blindSummary:
A 2025 anti-discrimination amendment (assented 30 October 2025; part in force 27 July 2026) removed the civil provision making it unlawful to 'offend, insult, humiliate or intimidate' a person in public on the basis of a protected attribute, including gender identity. This state/province is the only jurisdiction in this country that has actively reversed anti-discrimination protection rather than extended it; the government framed the rollback as 'restoring freedom of speech and religion.' For a visitor, public verbal abuse or humiliation directed at gender expression is now deliberately outside this state/province's law while other states have brought it inside.

Federal protections continue to apply uniformly: the federal sex-discrimination act of 1984 covers gender identity in every state/province, and hate-crime penalty enhancements for sexual-orientation- and gender-identity-motivated offences (a 2022 amendment, effective 2023) remain in force. No criminal expression ban, no facility-access ban, and no conversion-practice-specific enforcement issue arises for a short-term visitor beyond the general federal framework.

Remote-area context amplifies practical risk: a remote population centre records approximately 2,600+ offences against a population of ~25,000, and community infrastructure for trans people here is thin. A single domestic killing of an indigenous third-gender community member (in the state/province capital, October 2024) is recorded for completeness but is one non-patterned incident and does not support a regional violence finding on its own.

The deliberate legislative removal of the 'offend, insult, humiliate' protection is this country's only legislative rollback of anti-discrimination protection rather than an extension — a civil-law rollback rather than a criminal prohibition. In the same year, a neighbouring state/province moved in the opposite direction, creating a criminal offence for public incitement against a trans person.
blindSourceSummaries: Legislation page for the assented 2025 anti-discrimination amendment (assented 30 October 2025, part commencing 27 July 2026), which removes the civil prohibition on offending, insulting, humiliating or intimidating a person in public because of a protected attribute, including gender identity.

A national broadcaster (17 October 2025): the state/province parliament passes the rollback, with the government framing it as restoring freedom of speech and religion; the removal fulfils an election commitment against the previous centre-left government's 2022 expansion of the same protection.

A national broadcaster (2 March 2025): background on the provisions repealed — the 2022 act had made public offence, insult, humiliation and intimidation based on protected attributes (including gender identity) unlawful and had restricted religious-school hiring tests; coverage of the political fight over scrapping them.

State police, fire and emergency services community-safety statistics page for a remote population centre, the source of the high assault and offence counts against a small resident population used for the remote-area context.
A crowd-sourced legal-rights platform's regional page for this state/province: legal indicators and community safety ratings for the unit.
blindTangential: The removed civil provision protects every attribute (race, religion, sexuality, gender identity) — its repeal signals a broad de-protection climate; gender identity is one named attribute rather than the sole target.
blindOutOfScope: The high general assault statistics affect all travellers equally; they appear here only as thin-support and infrastructure context, not as a trans-specific mechanism.
